question: AgentCgroup argues a granularity mismatch (container-level policy vs tool-call-level dynamics) and aligns cgroups with TOOL-CALL boundaries. Is a tool call itself internally homogeneous in resource demand? If not, its own argument applies one level down.
finding: A tool call is NOT internally homogeneous. Within-call peak/min sampled RSS is 36x at the median and 586x at p90; a single call-level limit held for the whole call wastes 48.8% of the RSS resource-time envelope and 45.8% of the CPU envelope. CPU is bimodal: median 1.09x, so most calls are homogeneous, but p75 is 316x and p90 1811x.
limitations: COVERAGE IS THE MAIN CAVEAT: only 768 of 4203 multi-clause calls carry two or more non-null RSS values, and 272 for CPU. The dispersion statistics describe 18% and 6% of multi-clause calls respectively; the rest have unavailable clause-level resource labels.
Extreme ratios come from tiny denominators (a clause at ~0.001 MB), so the median is the load-bearing statistic and the max is not meaningful.

This is characterization, not a demonstrated system gain. Recovering the headroom requires that another tenant can use it, which is the same memory-pressure premise the KV lane is conditional on and which this corpus cannot exhibit.
Replay corpus; container and eBPF overhead inflate durations.
